You can follow the tutorial on that page for how to switch the boot drive: https://sensecraft.seeed.cc/ai-lab/zh/tutorials/rk/edge-ai-computer/rk3576/getting-start/recomputer-rk3576-flash-os#dd

entries.questionEn: How do I use GMSL cameras on the reComputer RK3576, and which deserializer works?
entries.directAnswerEn: Yes. The RK3576 can take GMSL cameras through an external GMSL deserializer adapter board. The deserializer converts the GMSL serial data into MIPI CSI-2, and the RK3576 receives it over its MIPI CSI interface; a MAX96712 is a suitable deserializer for this. H.265 hardware encoding and recording are supported as well: the RK3576 has a built-in VPU with H.264 and H.265 hardware encoding, and the chip specification reaches up to 4K at 60 fps.
entries.appliesTo: reComputer RK3576 boards with an external GMSL to MIPI CSI-2 deserializer adapter

entries.questionEn: How do I check the GPIO and the multiplexed pins of the reComputer RK3576 40-pin header?
entries.directAnswerEn: The 40-pin header can multiplex out up to 6 UARTs. Four standard UARTs (RS232, RS485 or KNX) are possible but require multiplexing and occupy 8 pins in total; one UART with CTS and RTS (MG24) is also possible; one CAN is possible, and the CAN on the 40-pin header is a native chip signal, so an external CAN transceiver is required for it to work. Because the multiplexing is extensive, functions such as SPI or I2C may not be available.
entries.appliesTo: reComputer RK3576 series 40-pin GPIO header, for hardware designs that plan UART, CAN, SPI or I2C multiplexing
steps: You can check the pin test and multiplexing status of the device in that wiki: https://sensecraft.seeed.cc/ai-lab/zh/tutorials/rk/edge-ai-computer/rk3576/interface-usage-guidelines/use-recomputer-rk3576-hardware-interfaces-and-fan-control#gpio

entries.questionEn: Does the reComputer RK3576 Industrial support a UPS and a TPM module?
entries.directAnswerEn: The device supports a UPS module, and that module is about to go on sale. For the TPM module, the RK3576 has a built-in hardware security mechanism, so no TPM module has to be added.
entries.appliesTo: reComputer RK3576 Industrial; the exact scope is confirmed together with the answer.
steps: Secure boot: the chip carries a BootROM code in ROM; at boot it verifies the digital signatures of the subsequent loaders step by step. The hash of the public key can be programmed into the one-time OTP memory or the eFuse of the chip for verification. Rockchip also provides tools such as rksecure to manage the secure boot state.
ARM TrustZone: the RK3576 supports ARM TrustZone, which splits the CPU and memory resources into a Secure World and a Normal World
The RK3576 integrates a dedicated hardware crypto module (Crypto IP) that supports the standard algorithms AES, DES/3DES, RSA, ECC and SHA

entries.questionEn: After a UPS module is added to the Raspberry Pi CM series products, the device does not power on when the power is restored immediately after a power cut. How should this be handled?
entries.directAnswerEn: This happens because, once the UPS module is installed, the function of the UPS overlaps with the shutdown logic preset on the CM5. When this occurs, simply power the device off completely and wait until the UPS has fully discharged; the device can then be started again.
entries.appliesTo: reComputer Industrial R20xx (based on the Raspberry Pi CM series compute modules), with a UPS module added and the device failing to power on when the power is restored immediately after a power cut
prerequisites: The probable causes of this behaviour are:
steps: The condition for a CM4/5 restart is that the voltage on the GLOBAL_EN pin stays low for more than 1 millisecond. The condition that pulls the GLOBAL_EN pin low is that the 5 V system supply drops below 1.65 V.

When the external power is cut, the UPS sends a shutdown signal to the CM4. If the power is restored before the UPS has fully discharged, the VDD_5_SYS voltage stays above 1.65 V, and at the same time the device has already received the shutdown command and has entered the shutdown state. In that case the GLOBAL_EN pin cannot go low, so the CM4 cannot restart.
notes: This only happens after a UPS has been installed; in normal use it does not affect the restart of the device. It only matters when the power fails suddenly, and then you have to pay attention to when the device is restarted (restore the power after roughly 10 to 20 seconds, or 1 to 2 minutes).
The situation can also be avoided by changing the shutdown logic in software; you can find the corresponding solution in the community: https://github.com/lucasnetau/ltc3350-ups

entries.questionEn: Does Seeed keep the IMEI and the LTE Cat 4 EC25 4G module serial number of the delivered reTerminal or reTerminal DM devices, and how can they be obtained when the device is already deployed and cannot be read on site?
entries.directAnswerEn: Seeed does not keep the IMEI and the 4G module serial number of the delivered devices, so these numbers cannot be filled in from the order, the product model or the host serial number alone. The IMEI and the 4G module serial number belong to the individual device or module and have to be read from the deployed device: the end user or the on-site technician opens the device serial console or the module AT command interface and runs `AT+GSN` to query the IMEI of that 4G module; the module serial number / module ID should be obtained from the module label or through the query command of the EC25 module. Match the query results one by one with the device asset numbers before completing the registration. If the people at the device location cannot be reached right now, the local end user or on-site technician has to run the queries and send the results back; Seeed cannot restore them from the original delivery records.
entries.appliesTo: reTerminal and reTerminal DM devices that have been delivered and deployed on site, for asset registration where the IMEI and the LTE Cat 4 EC25 4G module serial number have to be filled in
steps: Confirm the location, the asset number and the contact person of every deployed device.
The end user or the on-site technician connects to the device serial console or the 4G module AT command interface.
Run `AT+GSN` and record the returned IMEI; note that this command queries the IMEI and is not the same as querying the module serial number.
Query and record the 4G module serial number / module ID from the module label or from the command reference of the LTE Cat 4 EC25.
Match the IMEI, the module ID and the host asset number of every device one by one, and submit them to the device administrator to complete the registration.
If an on-site or remote connection cannot be arranged, the end user or on-site technician at the device location has to run the queries above.
successCriteria: The IMEI and the 4G module ID of every device have been read from the device side and registered against the asset number
The registration record contains no number that was guessed from the order or the host serial number

entries.questionEn: Can the device still be used when a part has come loose inside, is loose, or rattles? After a return has been requested, how are the inspection and the refund handled?
entries.directAnswerEn: If you find that a part has come loose inside the device, is loose, or rattles when the device is moved, stop powering and using the device immediately, so that a short circuit or further damage to the mainboard is avoided. Do not fit the part back yourself or continue dismantling the device; hand it over to technical support or the warehouse for inspection. When handling the case, take clear close-up photos of the outer packaging label (with the barcode), the device serial number (SN), the mainboard as a whole and the place where the part came loose.
entries.appliesTo: reComputer Industrial R21xx, for after-sales cases where an internal part has come loose, is loose or rattles and a return has been requested

entries.questionEn: Can the reTerminal DM operate at an ambient temperature of -20°C, and can an ODM version be ordered in a quantity of 10 units?
entries.directAnswerEn: The operating temperature range of the standard reTerminal DM is -10°C to 50°C, so the standard model alone cannot meet an ambient temperature of -20°C. Running at -20°C requires an ODM customization with a wide-temperature display or an internal heating solution. The minimum order quantity for an ODM customization is 50 units.
entries.appliesTo: The standard reTerminal DM, for projects that use the device at an ambient temperature of -20°C, and for ODM customization enquiries of 10 units

entries.questionEn: Does reComputer AI R2000 support a pre-configured hardware and firmware solution with an external GPIO, a built-in 26 TFLOPS Hailo 10 module and fanless cooling? Is there a standard or custom product that meets this?
entries.directAnswerEn: The enclosure of reComputer AI R2000 does not offer a general-purpose GPIO; it only provides interfaces such as DI/DO, RS485 and RS232. The currently recommended solution, the reComputer AI R2130-12, comes with an internal Raspberry Pi 40-pin GPIO and a built-in Hailo NPU.
entries.appliesTo: reComputer AI R2000 series and projects that need a custom pre-configured hardware and firmware solution

entries.questionEn: Can the reComputer ER1124-10 be replaced directly with a Laird/Ezurio BL654 (Nordic nRF52840) module and connected to an external antenna?
entries.directAnswerEn: The Laird/Ezurio BL654 cannot replace the on-board Bluetooth of the reComputer ER1124-10 directly. The Raspberry Pi CM4 used on that board already integrates Bluetooth natively, and the BL654 cannot take over the on-board Bluetooth of the CM4. If the BL654 and an external antenna are mandatory, the BL654 can only be designed as a separate external module. There is currently no BL654 external module or external antenna compatibility solution that Seeed has verified for the ER1124-10, so this cannot be treated as an upgrade option that Seeed provides or guarantees to be compatible. Before implementing it, you have to confirm the available board interfaces, the module connection method, the driver support, the power supply and the antenna layout, and complete the full communication and RF verification.
entries.appliesTo: reComputer R11xx series (reComputer ER1124-10 as an example), for cases that need to replace the on-board Bluetooth with a Laird/Ezurio BL654 or to use an external antenna

entries.questionEn: Can the reComputer R1124-10 (SKU 113991374) be used directly as a Zigbee network gateway? Is a separate Zigbee module mandatory, and can the on-board BLE replace it?
entries.directAnswerEn: No, it cannot be used directly. The Mini PCIe interface of the current reComputer R1124-10 does not support Zigbee, and the on-board BLE cannot act as a Zigbee radio. Although BLE and Zigbee both operate in the 2.4 GHz band, they use different wireless protocols and need incompatible hardware and software support, so the on-chip BLE cannot replace a dedicated Zigbee module. To use the device as a Zigbee gateway, a compatible dedicated Zigbee coordinator or module has to be fitted and connected through one of the host interfaces the device supports.
entries.appliesTo: reComputer R11xx series (reComputer R1124-10, SKU 113991374, as an example), for cases that need the device to be used as a Zigbee network gateway

entries.questionEn: Neither of the two USB-A 3.2 ports of the reComputer Industrial R21 recognizes a device and the boot log keeps showing error -71. How should the fault be scoped and handled?
entries.directAnswerEn: If the device shows a USB device descriptor read failure at about 0.8 seconds into the boot, keeps reporting error -71 (EPROTO) and finally prints "unable to enumerate USB device", and the USB5744 Hub is also not detected on the USB 3.0 bus, the hardware should be checked first. If the other units of the same batch work normally while only this unit keeps reporting the error before the user-space program starts, the fault can be attributed to a hardware failure on the USB 2.0 D+/D- signal path or on the hub circuit between the RP1 and the USB5744, rather than to an ordinary software configuration issue.
entries.appliesTo: reComputer Industrial R21xx, where neither USB-A 3.2 port recognizes a device and the boot log keeps showing error -71

entries.questionEn: Can the reComputer R1100 power external 24 V and 12 V sensors directly, and if 220 V, 24 V and 12 V have to be used at the same time, how should the power supply be chosen?
entries.directAnswerEn: The reComputer R1100 series does not integrate a dedicated power output for external 12 V or 24 V sensors, so those sensors need an independent power supply. If the application needs 220 V, 24 V and 12 V at the same time, you can choose a combination of independent supplies or a suitable multi-output power supply according to the actual load, but before selecting you have to confirm the rated voltage, current or power of the sensors, their polarity, the wiring requirements, the inrush load, the exact purpose of the 220 V and the electrical safety requirements on site. 12 V and 24 V sensors normally use a DC supply, so an industrial power supply matching those output specifications should be selected, adding a DC/DC converter where needed; a transformer should not be matched to the sensors on the voltage value alone.
entries.appliesTo: reComputer R11xx series (reComputer R1100 as an example), for applications that power external 24 V / 12 V sensors or use 220 V, 24 V and 12 V at the same time

entries.questionEn: Does the reComputer Industrial R21xx need an additional CAN transceiver to connect a CANopen angle sensor?
entries.directAnswerEn: The reComputer Industrial R21xx has an isolated CAN FD transceiver on board, so no additional CAN transceiver is needed. The CAN-H, CAN-L and signal GND of the sensor can be connected directly to the CANH/CANL/GND Phoenix terminals of the device. The sensor power has to be wired separately and must not be mixed with the CAN signal lines. A 120Ω termination resistor must be fitted at each end of the CAN bus; the R21xx does not have the termination resistors built in. The interface is compatible with CAN 2.0 and supports CANopen; it is mapped as `can0`/`can1` in Linux and starts communicating once the baud rate is configured.
entries.appliesTo: reComputer Industrial R21xx, for connecting fieldbus devices such as CANopen angle sensors through the on-board CAN interface

entries.questionEn: The reComputer Industrial R2245-12 has no HDMI output and the eMMC is not detected when flashing over USB. How should this be handled?
entries.directAnswerEn: After you enter BOOT mode and connect the board to the computer over USB, the system detects the eMMC of the R2245 automatically. First check in the Windows Device Manager whether an additional storage device appears, then use Raspberry Pi Imager to select the image and the target storage device and write it; if the option is available, rewriting a new image usually restores it. If the eMMC is still not detected, the eMMC or the CM5 may be damaged: you can open the enclosure, replace the CM5 and write the image again as a test; if the replacement succeeds, the original CM5 was damaged. Record the steps and the log during the test.
entries.appliesTo: reComputer Industrial R22xx (reComputer R2245-12 as an example), where the device has no HDMI output and the eMMC is not detected when flashing over USB
